_comment: HAND-DERIVED AS3 semantics for every case in ClosureCases.as. Never regenerate this file by running either arm: static field initialization is a language guarantee (a class initializer runs before the first static read), so the answers below follow from the source alone.
_derivation: AS3 initializes a class's static fields exactly once, before any static field or method of that class is used (AS3 language reference: static initializer / static properties). A closure does not change that: it is a value, and calling it reads the same static trait. So NAMES[1] is 'beta', NUMBER*2 is 14, TITLE is 'cases', Bag.NAMES[2] is 'gamma', PAIR[1] is 'y', the nested closure reads NAMES[0] = 'alpha', CFG.mode is 'cfg', Sealed.VALUE is 'block-set' (seeded by the static block), NAMES.length is 3 and NAMES.join('-') is 'alpha-beta-gamma'. Case 3 is the control: TITLE is a compile-time literal, so no initializer is involved and it must keep answering 'cases' on both arms.

label.1: closure reads OWN static const Array (bare name)
label.2: closure reads OWN static const int
label.3: closure reads compile-time literal String [control: no _cinit]
label.4: closure reads ANOTHER class's static Array (qualified)
label.5: closure reads a SECOND own static (shares one _cinit)
label.6: nested closure reads OWN static Array
label.7: closure reads OWN static Object literal, then .mode
label.8: closure reads a static seeded by a static{} block
label.9: closure read feeds .length (NULL slot would throw #1009)
